name: Financial Services & FinTech
heading: Money has been here before.
body: Every era of finance has had its jetpack. Double-entry bookkeeping. The telegraph. Electronic trading. Each promised speed and terrified the people who had to run on it, and each followed the same cycle: early adopters got burned, the tools didn't pay off until the institutions around them changed, and the firms that steered instead of braced wrote the rules for the next fifty years.

AI is finance's jetpack now. Models that price risk faster than any desk. Synthetic identities that pass KYC. Deepfake executives authorizing wire transfers. The technology is arriving faster than the trust infrastructure, and that gap is where the loss sits.
audiences: Banks, insurers, asset managers, fintechs, regulators, associations

forces.title: The authorization problem
forces.body: A voice on a call is no longer proof of identity. What replaces it, and how fast can you deploy it before the first eight-figure loss.

forces.title: Models nobody can interrogate
forces.body: Credit decisions that are more accurate and less explainable. Why regulators will force the issue and how to be ready.

forces.title: The trust premium
forces.body: When everyone has the same models, trust is the only durable differentiator. How the winners are building it now.

name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
heading: Medicine has been here before.
body: Every era of medicine has had its jetpack. Germ theory. Anesthesia. The randomized trial. Each one promised new heights and terrified the people who had to fly it. And each one followed the same pattern: early adopters got burned, the tools didn't pay off until the system around them changed, and the organizations that steered instead of braced set the standard for the next fifty years.

AI is healthcare's jetpack now. Diagnostic models that outperform specialists on narrow tasks. Synthetic patient data that can train systems without a single real record. Deepfake telehealth that can impersonate a physician or a patient. The technology is arriving faster than the trust infrastructure around it, and that gap is where the risk lives.
audiences: Health systems, pharma, payers, med-tech, associations

forces.title: The diagnosis trust gap
forces.body: Models that are right more often than doctors, and patients who still won't accept an answer they can't interrogate. Why accuracy isn't adoption, and what closes the gap.

forces.title: Synthetic everything
forces.body: Synthetic patients, synthetic records, synthetic trial arms. The upside is enormous. The perceptual security problem, deciding what's real, is the one no one is budgeting for.

forces.title: The workforce that stays
forces.body: Which clinical and administrative roles AI amplifies, which it absorbs, and how leaders keep the humans who make a health system worth trusting.

consortium.heading: The industry built it together.
consortium.body: Sam co-founded Chronicled, the company that convened the MediLedger Project and led the analysis behind the FDA's DSCSA pilot. Twenty-five organizations across pharma manufacturing, distribution, logistics, and retail pharmacy took part, covering the wholesalers responsible for the overwhelming majority of US prescription drug sales.
consortium.note: Final report submitted to the FDA, February 2020.

name: Future of Work
heading: Work has been here before.
body: The guild. The factory floor. The office. Remote. Every reorganization of how humans coordinate was a jetpack, and every one followed the same cycle: the tool arrived, the org chart didn't move, the productivity didn't show up, and then the organizations that redesigned work around the capability took the decade.

AI is the current one, and it arrived at the individual before it arrived at the institution. Workers save time on email and pour most of it back into the same meetings. That is not a technology problem. It is a redesign problem, and it is the exact chapter Sam's keynote is built for.
audiences: HR and people leadership, L&D, executive offsites, workforce and future-of-work conferences

forces.title: The job is not the goal
forces.body: People and organizations defend the current expression of their value instead of the value itself. Why that stalls transformation, and how to release it.

forces.title: Task, workflow, value
forces.body: Three levels of AI use. Almost everyone is on the first. The returns live two levels up, and the ladder for getting there.

forces.title: Capacity you already have
forces.body: Most capacity for change is occupied by what people refuse to release. Unlearn before you upskill.

name: Technology & AI
heading: Tech has been here before.
body: The industry that builds the jetpacks is the worst at steering them. Every platform shift, from mainframe to client-server to cloud to mobile, followed the same cycle: the tool arrived, the org chart didn't change, the productivity didn't show up, and then the companies that restructured around the tool took the decade.

AI is the fourth platform shift in forty years and it is moving faster than the three before it. The pattern still applies. The question is whether your organization is using it to do the old thing faster, or to do something that wasn't possible before.
audiences: Software companies, platforms, IT leadership, engineering orgs, developer conferences

forces.title: The productivity paradox, again
forces.body: Why the tools aren't paying off yet, and what changed the last three times they finally did.

forces.title: Org charts built for the old tool
forces.body: Every platform shift breaks a structure before it rewards one. Which structures break next.

forces.title: Building for expansion, not efficiency
forces.body: The difference between the companies that survived each shift and the ones that defined it.

name: Retail & Consumer Brands
heading: Attention has been here before.
body: Department stores. Catalogs. Big box. E-commerce. The printing press, radio, television, search, social. Every one of them was a jetpack, and every one followed the same cycle: the incumbents used the new channel to do the old thing, the challengers used it to do something new, and the gap between them became the decade's biggest transfer of value.

Generative AI is the current one, and it is the first channel that makes the creative itself. Generated influencers with real followings. Product photography with no product. Campaigns produced in minutes. Recommendation engines that shape demand rather than serve it.
The question isn't whether the machine can produce. It's what an audience will trust when production is free. The brands that steer this will own the next decade of consumer attention.
audiences: Retailers, CPG brands, e-commerce, travel retail, CMOs, agencies, brand and media teams

forces.title: Synthetic everything
forces.body: Generated influencers, reviews, and product imagery, with real audiences behind them. What happens to brand trust when the customer can't tell, and what disclosure is going to be required.

forces.title: When production costs nothing
forces.body: What becomes scarce when creative is infinite. The authenticity premium, and how brands are certifying the human hand.

forces.title: Demand you create versus demand you serve
forces.body: AI moved recommendation from responding to shaping, and personalization to a level that delights or alarms. Where that line actually sits, and the strategic and ethical consequences of crossing it.

consortium.heading: Proving what's real, at scale.
consortium.body: Before the keynote, Sam built the infrastructure. Chronicled, the company she co-founded, put cryptographic identity into physical products so a brand could prove an item was genuine without trusting whoever was holding it. The work ran with footwear and apparel brands facing counterfeiting at scale, and it is where the perceptual security argument she makes on stage started.
consortium.note: Chronicled clients and partners, not speaking engagements.

name: Hospitality & Travel
heading: Travel has been here before.
body: The steamship. The jet. The online travel agency. Each one collapsed distance and terrified the operators who had to absorb it. Each followed the same cycle, and each time the businesses that steered the change instead of resisting it set the standard for the era that followed.

AI is the current jetpack. Agents that book without visiting your site. Synthetic reviews. Dynamic pricing that outpaces your revenue team. The gap between the technology and the guest relationship is where the risk and the opportunity both live.
audiences: Hotels, airlines, cruise, travel retail, hospitality associations, destination marketing

forces.title: When the agent books, not the guest
forces.body: AI intermediaries are becoming the customer. What that does to loyalty, margin, and direct booking.

forces.title: Reviews you can't verify
forces.body: Synthetic reviews at scale, and what replaces the review as a trust signal.

forces.title: The human premium
forces.body: In an industry built on service, which human moments become more valuable as everything else automates.

name: Higher Education
heading: Universities have been here before.
body: The printing press. The lecture hall. The MOOC. Every one of them threatened to make the university obsolete, and every one followed the same cycle. Institutions that used the tool to do the old thing faster stagnated. The ones that reset on the real goal defined the next century of learning.
Generative AI is the current jetpack, and it arrived inside the classroom before anyone had a policy for it. The question isn't whether students use it. It's what a degree certifies when they do.
audiences: Universities, business schools, education associations, academic leadership, student events

forces.title: What a degree certifies now
forces.body: When the assignment can be generated, what exactly is being assessed, and what replaces it.

forces.title: Faculty as the differentiator
forces.body: Which parts of teaching become more valuable, not less, as content becomes abundant.

forces.title: Preparing students for a moving target
forces.body: Teaching for careers that will change three times, using a pattern that hasn't changed in five thousand years.

name: Government & Public Sector
heading: Government has been here before.
body: The census. The telegraph. The federal database. Every expansion of state capacity was a jetpack, and every one followed the same cycle: the capability arrived, the institutional trust lagged, and the governments that closed that gap kept their legitimacy.

AI and synthetic media are the current jetpack, and they arrive at the one institution that runs entirely on public trust. Deepfaked officials. Generated constituent mail. Election-grade disinformation. Steering this is not optional.
audiences: Federal and state agencies, national governments, NGOs, multilateral organizations, public-sector associations

forces.title: Legitimacy in a synthetic era
forces.body: When any official statement can be faked, what makes a real one credible.

forces.title: Service delivery at machine speed
forces.body: Where automation genuinely serves citizens and where it quietly excludes them.

forces.title: The procurement question
forces.body: Perceptual security is becoming a line item. What agencies should actually be buying.

logos: Agencia Nacional de Aduanas de México

name: Supply Chain & Logistics
heading: The supply chain has been here before.
body: The container. The barcode. ERP. Just-in-time. Every one of them was a jetpack that promised efficiency, and every one followed the same cycle: enormous gains, hidden fragility, a shock that exposed it, and then the operators who redesigned for resilience rather than pure efficiency taking the next era.
AI, autonomous logistics, and provenance systems are the current jetpack. Sam co-founded a company that brought trust to global supply chains, so this one is personal as well as pattern.
audiences: Manufacturers, logistics providers, retailers, supply-chain associations, procurement organizations

forces.title: Efficiency versus resilience
forces.body: Every optimization era ends in a shock. Designing for both instead of choosing.

forces.title: Provenance you can prove
forces.body: Counterfeits, gray markets, and verification as infrastructure rather than audit.

forces.title: Autonomy in the physical world
forces.body: Where autonomous logistics genuinely works and where the hype is running ahead.
